_comment: External research records: findings from targeted web research (2026-08-01) that answer or narrow open questions in the corpus. Official government sources (rva.gov, transportation.gov) are classified externally_verified; project-organization and news figures are classified reported_but_unverified. URL provenance is not file-verifiable and is counted as 'external' by the pipeline.
method: Targeted web searches against the open questions in data/unanswered_questions.json; official sources preferred; excerpts quoted verbatim from retrieved pages.

questionAnswers.answer: $16,000,000. The City's ARPA spending plan allocates $16M to the Southside Community Center ($8M in each of two fiscal years) — externally verified from rva.gov/arp and the ARPA Spending Plan PDF (ev:W-2). News coverage (Oct 2023) describes construction funding as 'mostly ARPA' plus roughly $6M in Council appropriations. Note: allocation, not final expenditure.

Aggregate mix externally verified (FY2025–29 proposed CIP): 64% general obligation bonds ($575M), 28% federal/state/regional transportation funds ($257.8M), 7% pay-as-you-go cash ($63.3M), 1% prior-year appropriations ($7.9M) — ev:W-4, flow f:cip-sources-fy25-29. Still unknown: which sources fund each individual project.

No City of Richmond RAISE/TIGER award was found. The City submitted a $40M RAISE application for the Fall Line Trail (2024), and USDOT's FY2024 RAISE grant agreements list contains Virginia awards (Rocky Mount, West Piedmont PDC, Suffolk) but none to Richmond (ev:W-9). Senators Warner and Kaine provided a $2M earmark to the trail. The corpus's RAISE/TIGER reference should be treated as an application/aspiration, not an award.

On the order of $120M+ as of late 2024 (reported, not an official budget figure): total cost anticipated >$400M (Apr 2024, CVTA via Richmond BizSense) versus ~$280M raised (Oct 2024, Fall Line quarterly meeting); CVTA is the largest funder at $124.5M (ev:W-8). No single official gap number was found; figures evolve with inflation.

The vendor and final schema are still not public, but the City's procurement solicitation (OpenGov project 100739, 'GPS Telematics Tracking') documents the required capabilities: real-time and logged tracking, nearest-vehicle dispatch, portable devices, and monitoring of plow up/down and sander on/off via PTO connections (ev:W-7). Any prototype schema should model those fields.

No awarded DPW fleet GPS vendor is publicly identified. The DPW solicitation (OpenGov project 100739) defines requirements including plow/sander status via PTO (ev:W-7). The Richmond Police Department separately uses Verizon Connect (since 2009) — a different fleet and system, not evidence of the DPW choice.

A structured residential sweeping schedule is published on rva.gov (12+ named routes with area names, date windows, and per-route map links; updated April 14, 2026) — ev:W-6. Machine-readable zone boundary GIS data was still not found.

The current-year schedule is published on the rva.gov street-cleaning page (ev:W-6); a historical archive of past schedules was not found. The Dec 2025 pause press release (ev:W-5) is one documented schedule disruption.

Richmond GeoHub (richmond-geo-hub-cor.hub.arcgis.com) exposes datasets with ArcGIS REST FeatureServer endpoints (e.g. services2.arcgis.com/V2PQwgZMTFfgM0Xu — RichmondCityRoads). A dedicated DPW transportation-projects layer was not identified by name; the CIP dashboard remains the project-level source.
